newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian minister demands action on corruption.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian minister demands action on corruption.

text.p: Corruption among government officials in Tanzania's coffee industry must be stamped out immediately, a government minister said.

Speaking at a closed-door inauguration of the board of directors of the Tanzania Coffee Board (TCB), Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Paul Kimiti called for greater transparency from TCB officials.

"Corruption must be fought on all fronts by instituting transparent procedures and improved management information systems in board activities," Kimiti said in the speech delivered on Wednesday and passed to Reuters on Friday.
"Transparency and accountability at all levels must stand out prominently in the image of your board."
While Kimiti did not offer any examples of corruption among TCB staff, he recommended the board consider improved pay and incentives as one way of battling graft.

"Routine surveillance, identification and flushing out of corrupt tendencies among staff will go a long way in winning the war on corruption. I am not ignoring the importance of bettering staff pay and incentives as another way of fighting corruption," Kimiti said.
Low pay and poor conditions among Tanzania's bloated state sector is a major cause of corruption, a situation acknowledged by the government.
Kimiti did not say how corruption had affected either the board's operations or the coffee sector in general.
